title: Zero foot drift does not prove skeleton-constrained motion cleanup
trigger: A cleanup stage directly overwrites one or more global joint positions during a contact interval and claims footskate/jitter improvement from zero foot drift.

currentObservation.note: The current preview locks only lfoot/rfoot horizontal XZ while tibia and toe points continue on their smoothed tracks. Zero locked drift is therefore true by construction but not a skeleton-valid cleanup receipt.

requiredInputs: joint topology or equivalent link set
declared cleanup stage and coordinate space
candidate bone-length sentinel with explicit scope
requiredMeasurements: root/hip reachability or explicit IK/FK feasibility
same metrics on at least one known-good and one known-bad control
candidateGate.passCondition: Drift reduction and skeleton-edge sentinel both pass on the exact subject; contact transitions and coordinate-space assumptions remain explicit.
holdConditions: zero drift is obtained by single-joint overwrite while adjacent edge sentinel fails
contact labels are unbound or silently guessed
only aggregate jitter decreases while topology/reachability is unmeasured
a method trained on another skeleton/domain is adopted without a bounded transfer trial

minimumFalsifiableTrial.hypothesis: Replacing direct foot-point overwrite with a kinematic cleanup route can reduce planted-foot drift without exceeding the candidate adjacent-edge sentinel.
minimumFalsifiableTrial.adoptionBoundary: One Animation/Humanoid Mother trial. Do not change R2 or global gates until an independent verifier repeats the exact-subject run.
